title_en: Chen Yixi — Application for Declaration of Unclaimed Property
keywords_en: civil; determination of ownerless property; first instance; basic people's court; Shanghai City; natural person; Civil Procedure Law; Inheritance Law; recognition of ownerless property; caregiver obtaining property; supporting plaintiff; inheritance of house; unclaimed; support obligation
full_text_en:
**Chen Yixi's Application for Declaration of Ownerless Property**

Applicant: Chen Yixi, male, born on June 14, 1948, Han Chinese, staff member of Shanghai Longtou Co., Ltd., residing at No. 10, Lane 323, Hejian Road, Shanghai.

The applicant, Chen Yixi, requested the declaration of the front half of the house at No. 12, Lane 323, Hejian Road, Shanghai as ownerless property, and sought an order vesting the said property in himself. The application was filed with the Yangpu District People's Court of Shanghai, the court of the place where the property is located.

The Yangpu District People's Court of Shanghai, in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China governing special procedures, heard the case with a single judge. Upon trial, the following facts were found:

The front half of the house at No. 12, Lane 323, Hejian Road, Shanghai, covering approximately 7 square meters, is a private house left by Chen Xiaomei, the applicant's paternal aunt. Chen Xiaomei died in September 1989. During her lifetime, Chen Xiaomei and her husband Xu Yuanlong (who died in June 1979) had one son, named Xu Shunlin (who died in January 1973). After the deaths of Chen Xiaomei's husband Xu Yuanlong and her son Xu Shunlin, the applicant Chen Yixi took care of her daily life. Chen Yixi provided substantial support to Chen Xiaomei.

In accordance with Article 175 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, on April 18, 1994, the Yangpu District People's Court of Shanghai issued a public notice at the court's bulletin board and at the location of the aforesaid property, calling for claimants to come forward. The statutory notice period was one year. Upon expiration of the notice period, no claimant appeared for the said property.

The Yangpu District People's Court of Shanghai held that the front half of the house at No. 12, Lane 323, Hejian Road, Shanghai, covering approximately 7 square meters, is indeed ownerless property and, according to law, should be vested in the State or the collective. However, given that the applicant Chen Yixi provided the main support to the original owner Chen Xiaomei during her lifetime, in accordance with Article 14 of the Inheritance Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "a person, other than an heir, who has provided more support to the decedent may be given an appropriate share of the estate," Chen Yixi should be awarded an appropriate portion of this ownerless property. Moreover, the value of this ownerless property is not substantial, and vesting it in the State or the collective would serve little practical purpose. Therefore, the applicant Chen Yixi's request to vest the said ownerless property in himself is in conformity with the law and should be upheld. Accordingly, on August 4, 1995, the court rendered the following judgment:

The front half of the house at No. 12, Lane 323, Hejian Road, Shanghai is vested in Chen Yixi.

In accordance with Article 161 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this judgment is final and effective.
